title: A middle order statistic is a median
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list in a linearly ordered set, and let $y$ be an element whose rank satisfies $\#\{z\in l:z<y\}<\lfloor(|l|+1)/2\rfloor+1$ and $\lfloor(|l|+1)/2\rfloor+1\le \#\{z\in l:z\le y\}$. Then at least half the entries of $l$, counting repetitions, are at most $y$, and at least half are at least $y$; equivalently, $|l|\le 2\#\{z\in l:z\le y\}$ and $|l|\le 2\#\{z\in l:y\le z\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $l$ is a finite list in a linearly ordered set
Fewer than $(|l|+1)/2$ entries are strictly below $y$, with the rank parameter interpreted as the integer quotient $(|l|+1)\mathbin{/}2$
At least $(|l|+1)\mathbin{/}2$ entries are at most $y$
